title: Oxidation calculations sheet
subject: Science
source: Seeded from science/y8 lesson 10 (Oxidation calculations sheet (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 10: Oxidation reactions. To understand oxidation as a reaction in which a substance gains oxygen

model.title: 2.4 g of magnesium burns to make 4.0 g of magnesium oxide. What mass of oxygen reacted?

questions.q: 3.6 g magnesium makes 6.0 g magnesium oxide. Mass of oxygen?
questions.model: Mass is conserved. Oxygen = product - metal. 6.0 - 3.6 = 2.4. So 2.4 g of oxygen reacted.

questions.q: Write the word equation for iron reacting with oxygen.
What two things does iron need to rust?
Core: Write word equations for copper, zinc and calcium reacting with oxygen.
questions.a: copper + oxygen → copper oxide; zinc + oxygen → zinc oxide; calcium + oxygen → calcium oxide.
questions.model: Teacher writes copper first: copper + oxygen → copper oxide. Metal + oxygen → metal oxide.

questions.q: Extend: 6.4 g copper gains 1.6 g oxygen. What mass of copper oxide forms?
Stretch: Explain why wood ash weighs less than the wood but magnesium oxide weighs more than magnesium.
questions.a: Wood's products are mostly gases that escape; magnesium oxide is a solid that keeps the oxygen it gained.

questions.q: Big question: why does magnesium get heavier but wood lighter when burned?
questions.a: Magnesium gains oxygen into a solid oxide; wood's products are gases that escape.
